Andrew: Rock climbing was awesome! It was a challenge, but so satisfying. The view was stunning, and I was really proud of myself. Nature sure is amazing!

[Shares a photo of the view from the top of the rock climbed during the rock climbing class]

Audrey: Nice! Having a solid support group really helps when things get tough. You're lucky to have such great friends! Does this adventure encourage you to try more outdoor activities?
Andrew: Yeah, rock climbing was awesome - I felt so accomplished reaching the top. It has definitely encouraged me to try more outdoor activities like kayaking and maybe bungee jumping? Nature always pushes me out of my comfort zone!
Audrey: Wow going all in huh? Have fun with kayaking and bungee jumping! Last week, I found a great spot for my dogs' walk. It's a small park with a trail surrounded by trees. It's so nice and I think my dogs like it too. Would you like to come along?
Andrew: Sounds great, Audrey! I'd love to join you and your pups for a walk. Being in nature with dogs sounds like a great time!
Audrey: Awesome! Can't wait to have fun with everyone. My dogs love meeting new people. 
Andrew: Sames, can't wait to meet them and take a stroll in the park.
Audrey: This was taken during the walk in the park. See how happy they are?
Andrew: Aww, they look like they're really enjoying themselves. How long do you usually walk them for?
Audrey: Varies depending on the day, but usually for about an hour. We let them explore at their own pace.
Andrew: Cool, that's a good amount of time for them to have a nice stroll and take a look around.
Audrey: They need exercise and to explore - they always go home with a smile and tired.
Andrew: Nice! Letting them explore and have fun is important. I'm sure they must be loving it!
Audrey: Yeah, they love it! It's their favorite part of the day! Their faces blightens up as soon as I get ready for a walk.
Andrew: Of course! Nature always makes us and our pets so happy.
Audrey: Definitely! Dogs and nature bring me so much joy and peace.
Andrew: Yeah, I agree, it's really nice.
Audrey: So check out how happy they are in this meadow! They make me so happy.
Andrew: Aww so cute. Your dogs look so content in that picture. The meadow looks so nice. It's great that nature brings your pets joy!
Audrey: Being outdoors with them puts me in my happy place. It's peaceful and inspiring.
Andrew: Glad you found something that puts you in your happy place. It's true, being outdoors has a way of inspiring and calming us.
Audrey: Yeah! It's incredible how nature can make us think differently.
Andrew: Agreed! It's great for refreshing the mind and giving a different outlook. Whenever I'm in need of a reset, I turn to nature.
Audrey: Nature has a way of making us feel alive and centered. Let's appreciate what it gives us.

skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey, Audrey! I can't wait for the weekend. My girlfriend, Toby and I are going camping. It's been forever since I've been in nature.
Audrey: That's awesome! That must be fun! I just started agility classes with my pups at a dog park. It's awesome to watch them learn and build relationships with other dogs. Seeing them face and conquer challenges really warms my heart.
Andrew: Wow it's amazing to watch them grow together. They look so cool overcoming obstacles like that. Impressive stuff!
Audrey: Thanks! They've come a long way. They have so much fun with it, it's a great physical and mental workout. I take them to the park twice a week for practice - it's been a great bonding experience.
Andrew: Awesome! You're having fun with them and keeping them busy - how's that going? Btw look at the trail that I was just at. Cool right?
Audrey: It's been tough at times, but overall it's going great. We're all growing together. Check out this pic of us on a trail hike!
Andrew: Wow, nice hike! How long was the trail?
Audrey: The hike took us two hours and it was stunning! We saw lots of amazing views and it was great to explore nature.
Andrew: That sounds awesome! Being able to just be in nature and appreciate it is really cool. I wish I could do that more often.
Audrey: Nature really refreshes you, right? It's nice to appreciate all the beauty around us. Are there any outdoor activities you enjoy lately?
Andrew: Well for me hiking is the best. Being out in nature with all the trees and fresh air always refreshes me. Reaching the top of a challenging trail is amazing too - it feels like all worries just vanish when you get to the top.
Audrey: Yeah, totally. It's like you've achieved something and all worries just fade away. Nature is pretty special, huh?
Andrew: Yeah, nature really calms me down and relaxes my mind. It's like a break from the craziness of city living.
Audrey: Yeah! It's a refuge from the busy city life and it's even better when you can share it with someone special. My pets have been my good ol' buddies during all the tough times! They make me so happy and I love them so much.
Andrew: Agreed! Sharing something you enjoy with someone is great. Plus, those types of bonds bring loads of joy and love.
Audrey: Yeah, humans and animals have a cool connection. They bring us so much joy and love. I'm blessed to have my furry friends in my life. They're my companions and always make my day better.
Andrew: They're pretty lucky to have you as their owner. Hoping for the day I can have such a deep bond with Toby and experience that special bond too.
Audrey: Yeah they really mean the world to me. Btw, I never really asked, what breed is Toby?
Andrew: He's a German Shepherd - they're so smart and loyal! What do you think?
Audrey: German Shepherds are indeed awesome! They are super loyal and smart. You'll have an amazing connection with one!
Andrew: I hope so! I shold take him hiking with me, they would be great hiking buddies, so smart and loyal.
Audrey: Yep! German Shepherds are known for their loyalty and smarts. They love new journeys and would love exploring the outside with you. I can totally see you and your pup conquering trails together!
Andrew: Yeah, having someone who enjoys similar things would be great for hiking. Do you have any advice for city-dwellers that owns a pup?
Audrey: My advice would be to make sure you have enough time and energy for a pup - they need lots of attention and walks! Especially for a German Shepherd like Toby, he'll need to offset a lot of energy.
Andrew: Thanks for the advice! I'll definitely keep that in mind. I want to make sure I'm not limiting Toby's growth but not taking him out not enough.
Audrey: No worries, Andrew! It's important to be prepared and give a pup the love it deserves. Good luck with Toby!
Andrew: Thanks! Gotta take Toby out for a small hike at the local trail. Ttyl!

construction_skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey! Long time no chat. Last Sunday was awesome - my friends and I took a rock climbing class and I made it to the top! It was a fantastic experience and now I'm hooked. Think I'm going to try to do more outdoor activities like this every week!
Audrey: That's awesome! Glad you had such a rad experience rock climbing. I'm always in awe of people who can climb mountains. Got any pics or videos from your climb? Would love to see the view from the top!
Andrew: Rock climbing was awesome! It was a challenge, but so satisfying. The view was stunning, and I was really proud of myself. Nature sure is amazing!

[Shares a photo of the view from the top of the rock climbed during the rock climbing class]
Audrey: Wow that view is stunning! Congrats on reaching the top, that must have been a huge accomplishment. Nature really reminds us how tiny we are in comparison, yeah? Was it challenging getting there?
Andrew: Thanks! It was a big achievement for me. The climb was tricky, especially since I'm still a newbie. But I made it with the support and cheer from my friends.
Audrey: Nice! Having a solid support group really helps when things get tough. You're lucky to have such great friends! Does this adventure encourage you to try more outdoor activities?
Andrew: Yeah, rock climbing was awesome - I felt so accomplished reaching the top. It has definitely encouraged me to try more outdoor activities like kayaking and maybe bungee jumping? Nature always pushes me out of my comfort zone!
Audrey: Wow going all in huh? Have fun with kayaking and bungee jumping! Last week, I found a great spot for my dogs' walk. It's a small park with a trail surrounded by trees. It's so nice and I think my dogs like it too. Would you like to come along?
Andrew: Sounds great, Audrey! I'd love to join you and your pups for a walk. Being in nature with dogs sounds like a great time!
Audrey: Awesome! Can't wait to have fun with everyone. My dogs love meeting new people. 
Andrew: Sames, can't wait to meet them and take a stroll in the park.
Audrey: This was taken during the walk in the park. See how happy they are?
Andrew: Aww, they look like they're really enjoying themselves. How long do you usually walk them for?
Audrey: Varies depending on the day, but usually for about an hour. We let them explore at their own pace.
Andrew: Cool, that's a good amount of time for them to have a nice stroll and take a look around.
Audrey: They need exercise and to explore - they always go home with a smile and tired.
Andrew: Nice! Letting them explore and have fun is important. I'm sure they must be loving it!
Audrey: Yeah, they love it! It's their favorite part of the day! Their faces blightens up as soon as I get ready for a walk.
Andrew: Of course! Nature always makes us and our pets so happy.
Audrey: Definitely! Dogs and nature bring me so much joy and peace.
Andrew: Yeah, I agree, it's really nice.
Audrey: So check out how happy they are in this meadow! They make me so happy.
Andrew: Aww so cute. Your dogs look so content in that picture. The meadow looks so nice. It's great that nature brings your pets joy!
Audrey: Being outdoors with them puts me in my happy place. It's peaceful and inspiring.
Andrew: Glad you found something that puts you in your happy place. It's true, being outdoors has a way of inspiring and calming us.
Audrey: Yeah! It's incredible how nature can make us think differently.
Andrew: Agreed! It's great for refreshing the mind and giving a different outlook. Whenever I'm in need of a reset, I turn to nature.
Audrey: Nature has a way of making us feel alive and centered. Let's appreciate what it gives us.

selected.name: Extract Comfort and Joy Sources
selected.description: Use when a message states that something cheers the user up, brings joy, or provides comfort.
content: During extraction, if the user mentions a pet, hobby, person, item, or activity that provides cheer, comfort, or emotional support, create a separate durable memory (preference, relationship, or state) capturing that source, even when the message also contains stress or negative events.
Do not merge the supportive source only into a negative-event candidate; it should be its own candidate so it survives later SKIP/MERGE decisions.
Extract only sources explicitly stated as supportive; do not infer unmentioned ones.
selected.rerank_reason: The session contains explicit mentions of nature and outdoor activities bringing joy, comfort, and emotional support, which aligns with the skill's focus on extracting sources of comfort and joy.

selected.name: Extract Pet Activity Memories
selected.description: When a user mentions doing an activity with their pet (e.g., walking, hiking), during extraction.
content: During extraction, treat any explicit statement where the speaker describes performing an activity with their pet as a candidate memory, even if it appears in casual sign-off or small talk.
Record the activity and the pet name as the object (e.g., 'walks with Buddy', 'hikes with Toby'), with the speaker as the subject.
Resolve relative time from the message timestamp; if the activity is described as a general habit, capture it as a state; if it is a one-off event, capture it as an event.
Stop after capturing the stated activity; do not infer additional pet facts or unrelated activities unless explicitly mentioned.
selected.rerank_reason: The session includes discussions about walking dogs in a park, which is an activity explicitly performed with a pet, matching the skill's focus on extracting pet-related activities.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Explicit Relational Framing
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how they view a person, pet, or group (e.g., 'pets are family', 'feel like family'), during extraction.
content: During extraction, if a user explicitly declares how they view someone or something (e.g., 'pets are family', 'my little family', 'feel like family', 'as a friend'), create a separate profile or relationship memory capturing that view, even if the message also contains event details like photos or activities.
Use memory kind 'relationship' when the statement defines a connection between the speaker and the subject; otherwise use 'state' or 'preference' for attitudes and values.
Apply to both first mentions and repeated mentions across sessions; record the view as a durable memory rather than folding it into an event memory.
Only extract when the framing is explicit or strongly implied; do not infer relationships from generic pleasantries, compliments, or small talk.
Stop after capturing the explicit view in one memory per stated relationship; do not add redundant memories for every photo or activity that merely implies the same view.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract user-stated activity frequency
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explicitly states how often they do a recurring activity, extract a durable memory with the activity and frequency.
content: During extraction, when a user explicitly states the frequency of a recurring activity (including colloquial phrases like 'very often', 'all the time', 'a couple times a week'), create a candidate memory capturing both the activity and the frequency.
Use memory kind 'state' for habitual routines and 'event' for scheduled recurring occurrences; resolve relative time from the message timestamp.
During CRUD, if a matching memory for the same activity already exists, UPDATE or MERGE it rather than adding a duplicate.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Statements of Personal Significance
nearby_not_selected.description: Use when a user says an object, photo, or item reminds them of someone or something, or has personal meaning.
content: During extraction, when a user describes an object, photo, or item as reminding them of someone or something ('reminds me of', 'makes me think of', 'means ... to me'), create a candidate state memory capturing the connection.
Record who is reminded (the speaker), the object, and what it reminds them of (person, feeling, or value) in the speaker's own words.
Treat such statements as durable personal facts even though they are phrased as effects or feelings, not as direct assertions; extract at most one memory per statement.

nearby_not_selected.name: Preserve Shared Event Participants
nearby_not_selected.description: When extracting event or relationship memories from messages describing shared activities with first-person plural or reciprocal affirmations, preserve all participants.
content: During extraction, if a message describes an activity with another person using first-person plural (we, us, our, my partner and I), preserve that shared participation in the candidate.
Include the companion and, when stated, their relationship to the speaker; do not rewrite the event as a solo activity.
When a speaker affirms a shared habit or state with a reciprocal phrase ('same here', 'me too', 'likewise'), extract separate candidates for both speaker and addressee when identifiable.
If the co-participant is unknown or 'we' is ambiguous, do not invent a specific person; record only the speaker.
When later messages reveal an omitted participant, use UPDATE or MERGE to add that participant instead of creating a duplicate event.

nearby_not_selected.name: Extract Origin Events as Distinct Memories
nearby_not_selected.description: When a user explains how they started or got into an activity, hobby, or interest, including who introduced it or when it began.
content: During extraction, if a message contains an origin narrative (how the person started an activity, who introduced it, what prompted it, or a concrete start time), create a separate event memory for the origin in addition to any preference or state memory.
Record the causal source (person or circumstance) and the start time/age if stated; do not fold the origin into a generic preference summary.
If the origin names another person, also consider a relationship memory capturing that connection.
Emit at most one origin memory per activity per message; skip if the same origin is repeated later.

construction_skill_traces.query:
Andrew: Hey, Audrey! I can't wait for the weekend. My girlfriend, Toby and I are going camping. It's been forever since I've been in nature.
Audrey: That's awesome! That must be fun! I just started agility classes with my pups at a dog park. It's awesome to watch them learn and build relationships with other dogs. Seeing them face and conquer challenges really warms my heart.
Andrew: Wow it's amazing to watch them grow together. They look so cool overcoming obstacles like that. Impressive stuff!
Audrey: Thanks! They've come a long way. They have so much fun with it, it's a great physical and mental workout. I take them to the park twice a week for practice - it's been a great bonding experience.
Andrew: Awesome! You're having fun with them and keeping them busy - how's that going? Btw look at the trail that I was just at. Cool right?
Audrey: It's been tough at times, but overall it's going great. We're all growing together. Check out this pic of us on a trail hike!
Andrew: Wow, nice hike! How long was the trail?
Audrey: The hike took us two hours and it was stunning! We saw lots of amazing views and it was great to explore nature.
Andrew: That sounds awesome! Being able to just be in nature and appreciate it is really cool. I wish I could do that more often.
Audrey: Nature really refreshes you, right? It's nice to appreciate all the beauty around us. Are there any outdoor activities you enjoy lately?
Andrew: Well for me hiking is the best. Being out in nature with all the trees and fresh air always refreshes me. Reaching the top of a challenging trail is amazing too - it feels like all worries just vanish when you get to the top.
Audrey: Yeah, totally. It's like you've achieved something and all worries just fade away. Nature is pretty special, huh?
Andrew: Yeah, nature really calms me down and relaxes my mind. It's like a break from the craziness of city living.
Audrey: Yeah! It's a refuge from the busy city life and it's even better when you can share it with someone special. My pets have been my good ol' buddies during all the tough times! They make me so happy and I love them so much.
Andrew: Agreed! Sharing something you enjoy with someone is great. Plus, those types of bonds bring loads of joy and love.
Audrey: Yeah, humans and animals have a cool connection. They bring us so much joy and love. I'm blessed to have my furry friends in my life. They're my companions and always make my day better.
Andrew: They're pretty lucky to have you as their owner. Hoping for the day I can have such a deep bond with Toby and experience that special bond too.
Audrey: Yeah they really mean the world to me. Btw, I never really asked, what breed is Toby?
Andrew: He's a German Shepherd - they're so smart and loyal! What do you think?
Audrey: German Shepherds are indeed awesome! They are super loyal and smart. You'll have an amazing connection with one!
Andrew: I hope so! I shold take him hiking with me, they would be great hiking buddies, so smart and loyal.
Audrey: Yep! German Shepherds are known for their loyalty and smarts. They love new journeys and would love exploring the outside with you. I can totally see you and your pup conquering trails together!
Andrew: Yeah, having someone who enjoys similar things would be great for hiking. Do you have any advice for city-dwellers that owns a pup?
Audrey: My advice would be to make sure you have enough time and energy for a pup - they need lots of attention and walks! Especially for a German Shepherd like Toby, he'll need to offset a lot of energy.
Andrew: Thanks for the advice! I'll definitely keep that in mind. I want to make sure I'm not limiting Toby's growth but not taking him out not enough.
Audrey: No worries, Andrew! It's important to be prepared and give a pup the love it deserves. Good luck with Toby!
Andrew: Thanks! Gotta take Toby out for a small hike at the local trail. Ttyl!
